claims.summary: For a monic polynomial F without real zeros, with u zeros above the real line and l below (n = u + l), F#(z) = conj F(conj z) and A_theta = F + e^{i theta} F#: if e^{i theta} != -1 then A_theta has degree n, at least |u - l| distinct real zeros and at most 2 min(u, l) nonreal zeros; if e^{i theta} = -1 it vanishes identically exactly when F has real coefficients, and otherwise has degree below n and at least |u - l| - 1 distinct real zeros.
claims.assessment: Working proof: on the real line A_theta = 2 e^{i theta/2} |F| cos(arg F - theta/2), the argument of F changes by pi (u - l) along the line, and the intermediate value theorem gives the real zeros; the degree bounds the rest.
claims.rationale: States what an interlacing count gives for a sum function of a configuration with zeros on both sides of the line: a count with an error of twice the smaller side.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; the count holds in 4000 random configurations of degrees 2 to 12, with the bound attained in 2245.
notes.significance: Context for the route: an elementary and presumably classical count. No novelty search beyond the registry.
notes.relationships: Complements the sign criteria for finite configurations, which characterize configurations on one side.

claims.summary: For T > 0 and 0 < eps <= T^2/4, F(z) = (z - i)(z - T + i eps) has one zero above the real line and one below, while F + F# = 2 (z^2 - T z + eps) has only real zeros (a double one at eps = T^2/4; at T = 20, eps = 100 the lower zero is 20 - 100i): one sum function with all zeros on the line does not place the configuration on one side, at any distance of the minority zero.
claims.assessment: Working proof by expansion of the product and the discriminant T^2 - 4 eps.
claims.rationale: Shows that real-rootedness of one sum function certifies nothing about the zeros it is built from, already for two zeros.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Explicit example verified by hand and numerically at three parameter pairs, one of them outside the range, where the zeros are nonreal.
notes.significance: Context for the route. No novelty search beyond the registry.
notes.relationships: The failure of the converse of the classical one-sided case of the zero count.

claims.summary: For a monic polynomial F of degree n without real zeros, A_theta = F + e^{i theta} F# and N(theta) the number of distinct real zeros of A_theta: (1/(2 pi)) int_{-pi}^{pi} N d theta = (1/pi) int_R |(arg F)'| dx = n - (2/pi) int min(P, Q) dx, P and Q the sums of |Im z_j|/|x - z_j|^2 over the zeros above and below the line; the mean is n exactly when all zeros are on one side, and if A_theta is real-rooted for almost every theta then all zeros of F are on one side.
claims.assessment: Working proof: the real zeros of A_theta are level sets of arg F, and the integral of the number of preimages equals the total variation; a multiple real zero occurs for finitely many theta.
claims.rationale: Decides the converse left open by one sum function: the whole family determines one-sidedness, and the mean number of nonreal zeros is an explicit integral.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.
